# Self-Contained Two-Part PDF Anthology — formatting contract

## Preliminaries (no full third section)

Use a compact cover page: passage, reader title, preparer, date, source count, navigation instructions. Add no more than 4 open exegetical questions. A **clickable internal** table of contents lists and links directly to every source start, and the PDF also has an outline/bookmark tree. Then deliver exactly two main parts in this order.

## PART 1 — COMMENTARY READING ROOM

A source entry should occupy a logical reading unit:

**SOURCE X — Author | Work | Passage location**

- "Why this is worth reading": one or two editorial sentences.
- Coverage label (EXACT / SURROUNDING / THEMATIC); edition/public-domain/copyright status.
- Original page/book URL and bibliographic information.
- **FULL RELEVANT ORIGINAL TEXT INSIDE THE PDF** in a comfortable reading font when the specific source/edition is public-domain, clearly reuse-licensed or supplied with adequate authorization. Distinguish full relevant units from longer contextual extracts. For copyrighted modern works without permission: do not reproduce the whole source; use short attributed legal quotations and substantial original navigational/exegetical analysis, plus a pointer to the original. Do not simulate a transcript by paraphrasing every paragraph.
- "Compare with": links to other source entries when they disagree or emphasize different aspects.
- "My observations / return to Scripture": 5+ blank lines or editable prompt area.

Preferred mix: 4–8 distinct relevant commentaries. Mark only the very strongest 1–4 passages per author; preserve their surrounding context so highlights remain intelligible.

**Shared mini-index:** interpretive distinctions **to investigate**, referring to authors, with no forced conclusion. Keep under half a page.

## PART 2 — SERMON WORKSHOP

Each selected full sermon gets a source card and a flow map:

**PASTOR | Full sermon title | Main passage | Date**
- Exact-passage label; verified official link; link to transcript and media if available; **content status: full manuscript / publisher outline / verified audio-video / metadata only / independent unverified transcript**.
- **One-line central rhetorical movement** (not a proposed user sermon main idea).
- **Sermon map** of 4–8 movements, in the preacher's actual order. Each move: textual anchor, *what the speaker does*, and actual transition where verifiable.
- **Illustrations/examples used in THIS sermon**, shown as separate inset lines or table rows:
  - Story/illustration: faithful 1–3 sentence description.
  - Kind: personal, historical, biblical, analogy, hypothetical, public claim.
  - Placement: opening/middle/conclusion or verified subheading/timestamp.
  - Purpose: what the illustration makes tangible.
  - Link back to biblical text: speaker's actual bridge, if present.
- **Landing:** how they concluded and invited response. Never describe vocal intensity, a pause, or emotional delivery if only written material was read.
- **Communication moves to notice:** no more than 3 concise observations; not a new outline imposed on user.
- **Reading/margin prompts:** What did the author see in the passage? Which moves would fit my congregation? Is this illustration verifiable / uniquely theirs?

2–5 genuinely read sermons, or fewer if sources are scarce. Embed historical public-domain original sermons in full when reuse rights for the edition are established; modern sermons receive manuscript-grounded analytical maps and illustrations, not illicit full transcripts. If the pastor has only mentioned the verse in a broader message, classify "partial reference", and give a very short source note; don't fabricate 4–8 movements about the requested passage. If only video/audio is available but wasn't actually examined, provide the direct watch/listen link rather than a fake sermon map.

**Optional closing comparison:** less than one page comparing each preacher's opening, structural logic, illustrations, biblical argument, and landing.

## PDF-first, iPad-friendly document mechanics

- **Downloadable PDF is mandatory by default** with a correct linked table of contents and native PDF sidebar bookmarks. A Google Doc can be an optional editable source but does not replace the delivered PDF.
- Keep body text at comfortable tablet size (approximately 11–12 pt), line spacing 1.3–1.5, ample white space.
- Use consistent named heading levels and native PDF bookmarks. Start passage/major parts on separate pages when possible. Ensure internal TOC links target the correct source heading rather than a prior mention of its title.
- Yellow highlight is for authentic source wording or especially valuable identified structural moves. Never highlight full pages.
- Visually label SOURCE TEXT, EDITOR NOTE, and READING QUESTION (don't merge them).
- Make all source-reference links clickable as supporting citations, but embed primary text when reuse is lawful. Give each author/book/sermon its own discrete block. Only add timestamp deep links when that exact recording position was checked; never guess seconds from transcripts that are not time-aligned.
- Note "complete original accessible by link" when a source cannot be reproduced.
- Don't create an unwieldy contents section larger than the notes it indexes.
- Do not add an AI-written sermon outline by default.

## Reader quality gates

1. Two parts visibly separated, commentary first; full source text legally eligible for inclusion must not be replaced by a website link.
2. Most page space is full legitimate public-domain/licensed original source reading (Part 1 and historical sermons in Part 2), with detailed transcript-grounded original flow analysis for copyrighted modern sermons; not general assistant theology.
3. Facts, quotes, narratives, and sermon movement claims supported by verified originals.
4. Unique illustrations and examples are concrete and attributable; no invented scenes.
5. Editorial analysis serves navigation and communication craft, not replacement of personal study.
6. PDF includes actual downloadable file, selectable/searchable text, clickable TOC, native sidebar outline/bookmarks, checked destination pages, visible highlights, page numbers and room for annotations.

## Explicit failure cases to avoid
- A short Google Doc giving mainly hyperlinks for reading → FAIL.
- A 3-page PDF that gives source names without substantive embedded historic text despite its availability → FAIL.
- A PDF with only nonclickable contents or bookmarks that jump to the wrong occurrence → FAIL.
- Claiming a full modern Piper/Keller/etc. transcript was embedded when it is copyrighted and permission was not granted → FAIL.
- Mixing text from 1 Samuel 22:1–5 and 23:13–18 as though Jonathan visited David at the cave → FAIL.
